summary: This script defines a greeting function and a main function that asks the user for their name, validates that they actually entered something (not just whitespace), and then either greets them or asks them to try again. The script only runs when executed directly, not when imported as a module elsewhere.

explanations.2: The f-string (the f before the quotes) lets you embed the variable name directly into the string using curly braces instead of concatenating it.
explanations.6: The strip() method removes whitespace from the beginning and end of the string; then the if statement checks whether anything remains (a non-empty string is truthy in Python).
explanations.11: This condition checks if the script is being run directly (as opposed to being imported into another script), which is a standard Python idiom to control when code executes.
